title: Connect intelligence and remediation
intro: Add your own provider keys to enrich scans of verified targets with breach, passive-DNS, and IP-reputation data. These intelligence connections are read-only. Cloudflare is separate: its scoped token can create or roll back an approved DMARC monitor-mode policy after you preview it.
connectionsBelong: Connections and provider usage below belong to {organization}.
requestedUnavailable: The requested organization is not available to manage. Showing {organization} instead.
adminRequired: Owner or admin access to an organization is required to manage connections.
signInRequired: Sign in as an organization owner or admin to manage connections.
verifyBeforeConnecting: Verify your email address before connecting or replacing a provider credential.
connectAdmin: Owner or admin access is required to connect.
dataSourcesBody: OUTSIDE sends only the verified domain or its resolved public IPs needed for the selected lookup. Provider keys stay server-side, encrypted at rest, and are never shown again after saving.
remediationBody: Unlike the read-only sources above, Cloudflare is a live write-capable connection. Its current scope is one guided workflow: preview, create, and roll back a DMARC monitor-mode TXT record for a verified organization domain.
cloudflareBody: Connect a token limited to Zone:Read and DNS:Edit. OUTSIDE shows the exact DMARC record before applying it and does not manage WAF, access policies, security headers, or other DNS records yet.
comingSoonBody: These connectors are planned, but cannot yet be connected from a customer workspace.
abuseipdbSummary: Flags addresses your infrastructure resolves to that have been reported for abuse, using your own paid-plan AbuseIPDB key.
awsSummary: Attributes discovered hostnames to your Route 53 hosted zones, so anything left unattributed stands out as a possible shadow asset. Read-only — the only permission needed is route53:ListHostedZones.
azureSummary: Attributes discovered hostnames to your Azure DNS zones, so anything left unattributed stands out as a possible shadow asset. Read-only — the Reader role is all the application needs.
censysSummary: Reports non-web services (SSH, databases, RDP, message brokers) observed on your resolved public addresses, using your own Censys API ID and secret.
digitaloceanSummary: Attributes discovered hostnames to the domains your DigitalOcean account holds, so anything left unattributed stands out as a possible shadow asset. Read-only — a read-scoped token is enough, and OUTSIDE never writes to your account.
fastlySummary: Attributes discovered hostnames to the domains your Fastly services serve, so anything left unattributed stands out as a possible shadow asset. Read-only — OUTSIDE never changes your Fastly configuration.
gcpSummary: Attributes discovered hostnames to your Cloud DNS managed zones, so anything left unattributed stands out as a possible shadow asset. Read-only — the DNS Reader role is all the service account needs.
githubSummary: Attributes discovered hostnames to the custom domains on your GitHub Pages sites — real external surface that is easy to forget. Read-only, and a read-scoped token is enough.
google_workspaceSummary: Attributes discovered hostnames to the domains your Google Workspace has verified. Read-only, through domain-wide delegation of the directory read-only scope; unverified domains are ignored.
greynoiseSummary: Tells opportunistic internet background noise apart from traffic that matters, using a commercially licensed GreyNoise key.
hibpSummary: Breach exposure for domains you have verified. Bring your own HIBP API key — used server-side only.
m365Summary: Attributes discovered hostnames to the domains your Microsoft 365 tenant has verified. Read-only — Domain.Read.All is the only permission needed, and unverified domains are ignored.
netlifySummary: Attributes discovered hostnames to the DNS zones your Netlify account manages, so anything left unattributed stands out as a possible shadow asset. Read-only — OUTSIDE never writes to your Netlify account.
openaiSummary: Generates plain-English explanations of findings using your own OpenAI key. Read-only over deterministic results — it can never add assets, findings or scores, and secrets and personal data are redacted before any call.
securitytrailsSummary: Finds subdomains that never appeared on a public certificate, using your own SecurityTrails API key.
shodanSummary: Adds one page of proprietary DNS context per scan (one documented query credit). Additional pages are reported as partial instead of fetched automatically.
vercelSummary: Attributes discovered hostnames to the domains your Vercel account owns, so anything left unattributed stands out as a possible shadow asset. Read-only — OUTSIDE never writes to your Vercel account.
virustotalSummary: Aggregates security-vendor verdicts on your domains, using your own VirusTotal API key. Requires a key licensed for commercial use.
